en: Haddab ibn Khalid narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Zakariyya was a carpenter."

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, they said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id informed me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is the most noble of people?" He said: "The one of them with the most Taqwa (God-fearing)." They said: "It is not about this that we are asking you." He said: "Then Yusuf, the prophet of Allah, the son of the prophet of Allah, the son of the prophet of Allah, the son of the intimate friend of Allah (Khalilullah)." They said: "It is not about this that we are asking you." He said: "Is it then about the origins of the Arabs that you ask me? The best of them in the pre-Islamic period of ignorance are the best of them in Islam, if they gain understanding of the religion."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said: I heard Abu al-'Aliyah saying: The cousin of your Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—meaning Ibn 'Abbas—narrated to me, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), he said: "It is not fitting for a servant to say: I am better than Yunus ibn Matta." And he attributed him to his father.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us—Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, he said: I heard Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrating from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that He—meaning Allah, Blessed and Exalted—said: "It is not fitting for a servant of Mine"—and Ibn al-Muthanna said: "for My servant"—"to say: I am better than Yunus ibn Matta (peace be upon him)." Ibn Abi Shaybah said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Shu'bah.

'Ali ibn Khashram narrated to us, 'Isa—meaning Ibn Yunus—informed us; (H) and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, both from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Anas; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sulayman al-Taymi: I heard Anas saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I passed by Musa while he was praying in his grave." And in the hadith of 'Isa, he added: "I passed by on the night I was taken on the night journey."

Haddab ibn Khalid and Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, they said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani and Sulayman al-Taymi, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I came upon—and in the narration of Haddab: I passed by—Musa on the night I was taken on the night journey, near the red dune, while he was standing praying in his grave."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Yahya, from his father, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not choose between the prophets (making some superior over others)." And in the hadith of Ibn Numayr: 'Amr ibn Yahya (narrated): my father narrated to me.

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to me, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Yahya, from his father, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, he said: A Jewish man came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) having been slapped on his face. And he relayed the hadith with the same meaning as the hadith of al-Zuhri, except that he said: "So I do not know whether he was among those who were struck unconscious and revived before me, or if the fainting at al-Tur was sufficient for him."

'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi and Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to us, they said: Abu al-Yaman informed us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: A man from the Muslims and a man from the Jews insulted each other... similar to the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Sa'd from Ibn Shihab.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Abu Bakr ibn al-Nadr narrated to me, they said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman and 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: Two men traded insults—a man from the Jews and a man from the Muslims. The Muslim said: "By the One Who chose Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) over the worlds!" And the Jew said: "By the One Who chose Musa (peace be upon him) over the worlds!" He said: Thereupon the Muslim raised his hand and slapped the face of the Jew. The Jew then went to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and informed him about what had happened between him and the Muslim. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not declare me superior over Musa, for people will be struck unconscious, and I will be the first to regain consciousness, and behold, Musa will be grasping the side of the Throne. So I do not know whether he was among those who were struck unconscious and regained consciousness before me, or whether he was among those whom Allah excepted."
And Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated it to me, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, with this exact same chain of transmission.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Hujayn ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: While a Jew was displaying some goods of his, he was offered something for it that he disliked or was not satisfied with—'Abd al-'Aziz was uncertain—he said: "No, by the One Who chose Musa (peace be upon him) over mankind!" He said: A man from the Ansar heard him and slapped his face, saying: "You say: By the One Who chose Musa (peace be upon him) over mankind, while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) is among us?" He said: So the Jew went to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, indeed I have a covenant of protection and a treaty." And he said: "So-and-so slapped my face." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Why did you slap his face?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, he said: By the One Who chose Musa (peace be upon him) over mankind, while you are among us!" He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) became angry until anger could be seen on his face, then he said: "Do not favor some prophets of Allah over others. For the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills." He said: "Then it will be blown into another time, and I will be the first to be resurrected, or among the first to be resurrected, and behold, Musa (peace be upon him) will be holding onto the Throne. So I do not know whether his falling unconscious on the day of the Mountain was reckoned for him, or whether he was resurrected before me. And I do not say that anyone is better than Yunus ibn Matta (peace be upon him)."
Abu Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, with the like of this hadith.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, he said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The Angel of Death came to Musa (peace be upon him) and said to him: Respond to your Lord." He said: "So Musa (peace be upon him) slapped the eye of the Angel of Death and gouged it out." He said: "So the Angel returned to Allah the Exalted and said: You sent me to a servant of Yours who does not want death, and he has gouged out my eye." He said: "Allah restored his eye to him and said: Return to My servant and say: Do you want life? If you want life, place your hand upon the back of an ox, and for every hair that your hand covers, you will live one year for it. He said: Then what? He said: Then you will die. He said: Then let it be now, close by! My Lord, cause me to die a stone's throw away from the Holy Land." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "By Allah, if I were there, I would show you his grave by the side of the road near the red dune."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—'Abd said: informed us, and Ibn Rafi' said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us—Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Angel of Death was sent to Musa (peace be upon him). When he came to him, he struck him and gouged out his eye. So he returned to his Lord and said: "You sent me to a servant who does not want death." He said: So Allah restored his eye to him and said: "Return to him and tell him to place his hand on the back of an ox, and for whatever his hand covers, he will have one year for each hair." He said: "O Lord, then what?" He said: "Then death." He said: "Then let it be now." So he asked Allah to bring him close to the Holy Land within a stone's throw. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "So if I were there, I would show you his grave by the side of the road beneath the red dune."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us, Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) never lied except for three lies, two of which were for the sake of Allah: his statement, 'Indeed, I am sick,' and his statement, 'Rather, this largest of them did it'; and one regarding Sarah. For he came to the land of a tyrant, accompanied by Sarah, and she was the most beautiful of people. He said to her: 'Indeed, if this tyrant knows that you are my wife, he will overpower me to take you. So if he asks you, tell him that you are my sister, for you are my sister in Islam, and I know of no Muslim on earth besides me and you.' When he entered his land, some of the tyrant's people saw her and went to him, saying to him: 'A woman has entered your land whom no one ought to have but you.' So he sent for her, and she was brought. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) stood up to pray. When she entered upon him, he could not restrain himself from reaching out his hand toward her, but his hand was seized with a severe seizure. He said to her: 'Pray to Allah to release my hand, and I will not harm you.' So she did, but he returned to it, and it was seized even more severely than the first seizure. He said to her the like of that, so she did, but he returned to it, and it was seized even more severely than the first two seizures. He said: 'Pray to Allah to release my hand, and by Allah I swear to you that I will not harm you.' So she did, and his hand was released. He called the one who had brought her and said to him: 'You have brought me a devil, not a human being! Drive her out of my land and give her Hajar.' He said: So she came walking back, and when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saw her, he finished praying and said to her: 'What is the news?' She said: 'Good! Allah restrained the hand of the wicked one and gave us a servant.' Abu Hurayrah said: "That is your mother, O sons of the water of the sky!"

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Mughirah—meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hizami—narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was circumcised when he was eighty years old with an adze."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Mukhtar, he said: I heard Anas narrate from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) the like of it.

And Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: I heard Mukhtar ibn Fulful, the freed slave of 'Amr ibn Hurayth, saying: I heard Anas saying: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah..." with the like of it.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Mushir and Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Mukhtar; (H) and 'Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di narrated to me—and the wording is his—'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, al-Mukhtar ibn Fulful informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O best of creation!" So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "That is Ibrahim (peace be upon him)."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, he said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "'Isa ibn Maryam saw a man stealing, so 'Isa said to him: 'Did you steal?' He said: 'By no means, by the One other than Whom there is no god!' So 'Isa said: 'I believe in Allah, and I have disbelieved my own eyes.'"

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah informed us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The cry of the newborn when it is delivered is from a pricking of Satan."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me, that Abu Yunus, Sulaym, the freed slave of Abu Hurayrah, narrated to him from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "Every one of the children of Adam is touched by Satan on the day his mother gives birth to him, except for Maryam and her son."

And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated it to me, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us; (H) and 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to me, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, all from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, and both of them said: "He touches him when he is born, so he begins screaming from Satan touching him." And in the hadith of Shu'ayb: "from the touch of Satan."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "There is no newborn who is born except that Satan pricks him, so he begins screaming from the pricking of Satan, except for the son of Maryam and his mother." Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite if you wish: {And indeed, I seek refuge with You for her and for her offspring from the accursed Satan.}"

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, he said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I am the closest of people to 'Isa ibn Maryam in this worldly life and in the Hereafter." They said: "How is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The prophets are brothers from co-wives, their mothers are different, and their religion is one, and there is no prophet between us."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Dawud, 'Umar ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I am the closest of people to 'Isa. The prophets are brothers from co-wives, and there is no prophet between me and 'Isa."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Abu Salamah informed him that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saying: "I am the closest of people to the son of Maryam. The prophets are brothers from co-wives, and there is no prophet between me and him."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, he said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—and he mentioned several hadiths, among which: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, a day will surely come upon one of you when he will not see me, then that he should see me would be dearer to him than his family and his wealth along with them." Abu Ishaq said: The meaning of it according to me is: that he should see me along with them would be dearer to him than his family and his wealth, and it is in my view transposed.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us, both from al-Aswad ibn 'Amir—Abu Bakr said: Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us—Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, and from Thabit, from Anas, that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed by some people pollinating date palms, so he said: "If you were not to do it, it would still come out right." He said: But it yielded unpollinated dates. He passed by them again and said: "What is the matter with your date palms?" They said: "You said such and such." He said: "You know better regarding the affairs of your worldly life."
